AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: The aim was to compare the effectiveness of chewing sugar-free gum after bowel resection on bowel function and length of stay.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: Randomised controlled trial of patients undergoing elective open or laparoscopic bowel surgery, allocated into two groups, a chewing gum group (CG) or a non-chewing gum group (NG). Primary outcomes were time to discharge (LOS), time to first flatus (TFF) and time to first bowel motion (TBM). Secondary outcomes were complication rates, pain and total morphine equivalent (TMEq) medication for seven days after the procedure.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Between 2010-2013, 162 patients were randomised, 4 excluded (82 in CG, 76 in NG). There was no difference in the LOS between the CG (5.8 days) and the NG (6.1 days, P = 0.403), or TFF between the CG (42.0 median hours) and the NG (58.0 median hours, P = 0.076). The TBM was lower in the CG (40.0 median hours) compared to the NG (90.0 median hours, P = 0.002). There was no difference in intraoperative complications between the CG (9%) and the NG (9%, P = 0.901), or early postoperative complications (CG (44%), NG (55%), P = 0.131). There was no difference in TMEq at 24 hours post procedure, but the CG had reduced TMEq from days 2 to 7 post procedure, and 7 day total. Pain was higher among NG at day three.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Chewing sugar-free gum resulted in an earlier return to bowel function and decreased analgesic requirements. There was no decrease in overall length of stay or post-operative complications. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
